title: Jason Cohen's Fairytale Plan: quarterly strategic planning in five parts
summary: Jason Cohen shows how to build a quarterly strategic plan using the fairytale story structure: Objectives, Obstacles, Actions, Measures, and Not Doing. He argues most planning time belongs on defining obstacles, picking a few big "rocks," and stating out loud what you are choosing not to do.

principles.text: Structure a strategic plan as a story: objectives, obstacles, actions, measures, and what you're not doing.
principles.quote: Our brains are pre-wired for fairy-tales, so we naturally follow the presentation as it flows into those primordial ruts in our gray matter.

principles.text: Spend most planning time on obstacles; don't jump to solutions before fully exploring the problem.
principles.quote: Without fully exploring the problem-space, you're not in a position to even know the goal of the solution-space.

principles.text: Narrow obstacles to the 1-3 that, if solved, would unlock the objectives even if everything else festered.
principles.quote: Narrow these down to 1-3 most critical issues.

principles.text: When obstacles are serious, prioritize in order: retention, people, throughput, growth, competition, code health, execution risk.
principles.quote: 1. Retention (if customers are leaving, the business model and product isn't working)

principles.text: Pick a few big, impactful 'rocks' rather than incremental work; judge by impact on critical things, not ROI.
principles.quote: For your most critical pieces of work, the goal is not to optimize your time, but rather to maximize your impact on the most critical things.

principles.text: Publish a 'Not Doing' list: most deferred items are really 'not ever', and saying so keeps the team focused.
principles.quote: When you don't articulate what we're not doing, it can appear that you don't even know those things exist.
